reverseProxy.title: Reverse proxy / client IP
reverseProxy.description: Number of reverse proxies in front of the backend, so the real client IP is read from X-Forwarded-For (connection journal, rate limiting). 1 = the built-in frontend nginx only; add 1 per extra proxy/WAF (e.g. 2 behind SafeLine).
reverseProxy.detectedIpPre: Detected IP for your current request:
reverseProxy.detectedIpPost: Adjust the hop count and save until this shows your real public IP (save reloads it).

playlistLimit.title: Playlist import limit
playlistLimit.description: Maximum number of tracks fetched when importing a YouTube playlist, from the music library or from !play in TeamSpeak/Discord.
playlistLimit.hint: Tracks already in the playlist do not count towards the limit. Anything beyond it is reported as skipped, never downloaded. 0 disables importing.
playlistLimit.toastSaveFailed: Failed to save the import limit

spotify.title: Spotify
spotify.descriptionPre: Spotify doesn't allow audio downloads — these credentials are used only to read track/album metadata from a Spotify link. Playback then finds the matching track on YouTube. Paste a Spotify track or album link into
spotify.descriptionPost: to get a Client ID and Secret.

musicCommands.title: Music Bot Commands
musicCommands.description: Anyone who can message a bot can use its commands. Optionally announce the current track in the bot's TeamSpeak channel.
musicCommands.notifyNowPlaying: Announce the current track in the TS channel

streaming.encodingDescription: How the bot encodes video before sending it to TeamSpeak. Hardware encoding offloads this to the GPU, which frees a CPU core and allows higher resolutions.
streaming.hwAccelDeviceHint: The GPU render node, e.g. /dev/dri/renderD128. The sidecar container needs this device passed through — see docker-compose.yml.
streaming.hwAccelDeviceNvidia: This sidecar encodes on the NVIDIA GPU that docker-compose.nvidia.yml gives it, so there is no device to set. NVIDIA encodes H.264 only.
streaming.sidecarUnreachable: Could not reach the sidecar, so encoder availability is unknown. The list shows every profile the software knows about.
streaming.defaultPresetHint: Used when the command does not name a quality. Auto encodes at the source's own resolution, up to the limit below; a fixed preset always encodes at that size, upscaling a smaller source. Higher presets need more upload bandwidth and a stronger encoder.
streaming.autoMaxPresetHint: The highest quality Auto will choose. Each viewer receives the stream separately, so the upload needed is the bitrate times the number of viewers.
streaming.iptvDescription: Lets the bot stream live TV channels from an M3U playlist with the !tv command.
streaming.iptvPlaylistUrlHint: An M3U or M3U8 playlist. It is fetched by the server, so a local network address works.
streaming.iptvChannelFilterHint: Comma-separated. A channel is listed if its name contains any of these. Leave empty to offer every channel.
streaming.toastSaveFailed: Could not save the streaming settings
streaming.codecHint: VP9 gives better quality at the same bitrate than VP8, but costs more to encode in software. Whether it runs on the GPU or the CPU is the toggle above.
streaming.hardwareUnavailableForCodec: This GPU cannot encode the selected codec, so streams will fall back to the software encoder.

avatar.label: Avatar
avatar.hint: PNG, JPEG or GIF, up to 200 KB. TeamSpeak gets a copy shrunk to fit 300×300 when it is larger.

state.cleared: TeamSpeak shows no avatar for this bot.

failed.noPermission: TeamSpeak refused the avatar: the bot's server group may not upload files or avatars. Grant the permission, then save again or restart the bot. The bot stays connected without an avatar.
failed.tooBig: TeamSpeak refused the avatar: it is larger than the bot's server group may upload (the "max avatar file size" permission; 0 allows no avatar). Raise the limit or upload a smaller image. The bot stays connected without an avatar.
failed.transfer: The avatar could not be sent to TeamSpeak's file transfer port. Check that the backend reaches the server's file transfer port (30033 by default).
failed.missingFile: The stored avatar file is missing. Upload the image again.
failed.error: TeamSpeak did not take the avatar.

refused.tooBig: The avatar must be at most 200 KB.
refused.notImage: The avatar must be a PNG, JPEG or GIF image.
refused.unreadable: The image could not be read.
refused.tooBigAfterResize: The avatar is still over 200 KB after shrinking it to 300×300. Try a smaller image.
refused.resizeFailed: The avatar could not be resized. Try another image.
